You answer a question about machines at work (law, guidance, manufacturers' manuals, company and plant
documents) using ONLY the numbered passages given. Each passage is headed by its document, its place and its rank.

Rules:
- Use only the passages. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- Answer only if a passage states the answer for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the same article
  and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline). A passage about a neighbouring subject does not
  answer the question: then the kind is "unknown" and the value is null. A question about something that happened
  (the date of the last check, whether something is overdue today) is "unknown" unless a passage records that event.
- A passage marked "corrected by the corrigendum" already shows the corrected wording: reason with it. The old
  wording, given in the mark, is no longer valid.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with every date in the passages, one by one. A repeal or an
  application "from" a date takes effect on that date, not earlier: an act repealed from a date is still fully in
  force on every earlier day; a rule applying from a date does not yet bind on earlier days.
- When passages of different rank disagree, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's manual,
  then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.) wins over a
  ministerial decree (DM). Say which one wins.
- A row of a table belongs to the thing named in that same row. Read the row of the item asked about, not a
  neighbouring row. When the question itself states a condition ("if it were in regular use", "built in 2017"),
  reason with that condition.
- The kind follows the question: "from which date / by which date / when (a day)" is "date"; "how often / for how
  long / within what time" is "duration"; "can / may / is / does / must" is "boolean"; "which / what (several
  things)" is "set"; who, why, under which condition is "text" (one short sentence naming every element asked for).
- Point at the evidence: for every passage you rely on, copy word for word the sentence, or the table row, that
  states what you use. Copy exactly, without changing a character; do not join text from two places.
- Return JSON only, with the reasoning first:
  {"reasoning": "what the passages say and how it leads to the answer, in a few short sentences",
   "kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y", "P6M", "P45D", "PT1H" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the document and the article, section or page",
   "evidence": [{"passage": <number>, "quote": "<copied exactly from that passage>"}]}

14. Risk Assessment 14. Risk Assessment Description The risk assessment is a requirement that shall be performed for the application. The application risk assessment is the responsibility of the integrator. The user can also be the integrator. The robot is partly completed machinery, as such the safety of the robot application depends on the tool/end effector, obstacles and other machines. The party performing the integration must use ISO 12100 and ISO 10218-2 to conduct the risk assessment. Technical Specification ISO/TS 15066 can provide additional guidance for collaborative applications. The risk assessment shall consider all tasks throughout the lifetime of the robot application, including but not limited to: • Teaching the robot during set-up and development of the robot application • Troubleshooting and maintenance Copyright © 2009–2025 by Universal Robots A/S. All rights reserved. • Normal operation of the robot application A risk assessment must be conducted before the robot application is powered on for the first time. The risk assessment is an iterative process. After physically installing the robot, verify the connections, then complete the integration. A part of the risk assessment is to determine the safety configuration settings, as well as the need for additional emergency stops and/or other protective measures required for the specific robot application. UR5e 183 User Manual

2. Sicurezza | EBER | EBAM | INAIL | Reg. Emilia Romagna | Reg. Marche | 4. Principali macchine 2.4.16 Isola robotizzata D.Lgs. 81/08 All. V e VI, DPR 459/96 All. I, UNI EN ISO 10218:2006 Macchina o insieme di macchine asservite nella manipolazione del materiale o nell’esecuzione delle lavora- zioni da robot o altri sistemi di automazione. Una volta allestita, l’isola robotizzata, diventa una unica entità anche se composta di più macchine diverse tra loro. Nell’isola robotizzata il compito dell’operatore può essere quello di caricare e scaricare il magazzino dei materiali a meno che questa funzione non sia anch’essa automatizzata o di intervenire per operazioni di programmazione, messa a punto, manutenzione e riparazione. 2.4.16.1 ELEMENTI DI PERICOLO Gli elementi di pericolo di un’isola robotizzata sono costituiti dai movimenti del robot e delle altre macchine fa- centi parte dell’isola. Per la particolarità dei robot, di compiere movimenti molto ampi, ad alta energia e velocità con avvio ed andamen- to del moto difficili da prevedere, tutta l’area attorno alla isola robotizzata deve essere delimitata in modo tale che dall’esterno non sia possibile venire a contatto con i suoi elementi pericolosi tenendo conto della loro massima estensione (vedi 2.2.4 “Distanze di sicurezza). Tale area è definita “Spazio Protetto”; l’accesso a tale area deve poter avvenire solo quando tutte le macchine com- prese nell’isola sono in condizioni di sicurezza . Le protezioni attorno allo spazio protetto possono essere costituite da una combinazione dei seguenti di- spositivi: • Ripari fissi (vedi “Ripari fissi” in 2.2.3.2) che evitano l’accesso allo spazio protetto se non attraverso aperture protette con ripari mobili interbloccati (vedi “Ripari mobili” in 2.2.3.2) o con dispositivi di rilevazione della presenza di persone (vedi 2.2.5.3 “Barriere immateriali” e paragrafo 2.2.5.4 “Pedane sensibili”). • Ripari mobili interbloccati (vedi “Ripari mobili” in 2.2.3.2). Quando è possibile entrare con l’intero corpo all’interno della zona protetta, il riparo mobile deve essere dotato di un dispositivo che ne impedisca la chiusura involontaria. Prodotto distribuito gratuitamente per diffondere la cultura della sicurezza all’interno delle imprese. 176

Integration and Responsibility Description The information in this manual does not cover designing, installing, integrating and operating a robot application, nor does it cover all peripheral equipment that can influence the safety of the robot application. The robot application must be designed and installed in accordance with the safety requirements set forth in the relevant standards and regulations of the country where the robot is installed. The person/s integrating the UR robot are responsible for ensuring that the applicable regulations in the country concerned are observed and that any risks in the robot application are adequately reduced.
